artworks.title: Silver Didrachm (Stater) of the Aetolian League: Aetolus Resting by a Rock
artworks.description: This Hellenistic silver didrachm struck by the Aetolian League depicts the federation's mythical eponym, Aetolus, the son of Endymion who fled the Peloponnese after a fatal chariot mishap and gave his name to the land of Aetolia. The hero is shown as a youthful warrior at rest, seated against a rock with his lance and sword, a heroic hunter type that the Aetolian confederacy adopted as its civic emblem. The choice of Aetolus on state coinage was a deliberate genealogical claim: by minting their founder onto their money, the Aetolians declared their region's identity to be rooted in his myth. Numismatic Museum of Athens.

artworks.title: Silver Drachm of the Aetolian League: Artemis and Aetolus Enthroned on Shields
artworks.artist: Unknown (Aetolian League mint, Munich State Coin Collection)
artworks.description: On the reverse of this silver drachm of the Aetolian League, the eponymous hero Aetolus (Aitolos) is enthroned upon a heaped pile of captured Macedonian and Gallic shields, holding a spear, beside the league legend ΑΙΤΩΛΩΝ; the obverse bears the laureate head of Artemis with bow and quiver. The image fuses myth and politics: Aetolus, ancestral founder of the Aetolian people, presides in triumph over the arms of the Gauls defeated when they were repulsed from Delphi in 279 BC, the victory that made the league a great power. Minting their founder as a warrior atop spoils, the Aetolians turned their distant mythic eponym into a living symbol of federal strength. Staatliche Münzsammlung, Munich.
